correctness.rationale: The submitted Finding asserts the upper f-divergence equality case forces the specific lower Frechet-Hoeffding diagonal even though the divergence identity and bound explicitly do not require diagonal convexity. This is false: for d=2 put q(u)=2 on [1/4,3/8] and [5/8,1], and q=0 elsewhere, and Delta(u)=integral_0^u q. Then Delta(1)=1, Delta(u)<=u, and 0<=Delta(v)-Delta(u)<=2(v-u), so Cattaneo et al. Lemma 1 makes it an attainable copula diagonal. For strictly convex phi (in particular phi(t)=t log t), q in {0,2} achieves the upper bound KL=log 2, yet Delta(3/8)=1/4 while max(2*(3/8)-1,0)=0. The proof and REVIEW.md partly acknowledge uniqueness only inside the diagonally convex subclass; the unqualified Finding is scientifically false. Density-ratio likelihood-order iff, information identity, and numerical envelope are otherwise correct.
